Q: How do you know if you truly understand a concept? A:

The difference between understanding and memorization is what happens when you encounter a problem that you've never encountered before.

Understanding will allow you to solve the problem. Memorization won't.

How do you know if you have just memorized something? By testing yourself on different problems.

But having said that, many CS concepts (and principles) are kind of "wobbly". The harder you think about them and try to apply them, the more you come to realize that they don't have much depth to them and/or they don't apply in lots of cases.

You also need to set your expectations appropriately. You shouldn't expect your CS course is going to give you the same depth of understanding of the concepts as (say) a developer with many years of programming experience.

Q: HttpOnly always set to true on cookie I add A:

I ran into the same issue in aspnet Core, in our case it was because of a cookie policy set by UseCookiePolicy.

The HttpOnly property was set to HttpOnlyPolicy.Always.

If you need to bypass the policy, you can manually set the header using HttpContext.Response.Headers.

You then have to provide all properties of the cookie:

HttpContext.Response.Headers.SetCookie = $"{AuthTokenName}={result.AccessToken}; samesite=none; strict; path=/;"; // + ... max-age, expires...

See Set-Cookie header syntax.

Q: valgrind --tool=massif` crashes with SIGTRAP inside `pthread_cond_timedwait` on RHEL9/glibc 2.34 A:

Valgrind never injects int3. Something else is going that.

I've seen a similar issue with systems that use TaniumClient. The problem could be something like bpftrace (see the last item in the link). Otherwise it could be due to whatever your kubernetes pod is doing.

A also expect that this is not limited to Valgrind. If you run your test exe in gdb do you also get a SIGTRAP?

massif only redirects malloc and operator new (and their related C and C++ families). The redirect for DRD is not loaded by massif.
